sentences.text: Lee Whitfield (client) disclosed he lost his job in January at the depot.
Lee Whitfield stated the housing element of Universal Credit went wrong, causing rent to build up.
Lee Whitfield disclosed arrears of £3,850, estimated to be for three or four months.
Lee Whitfield stated he received court papers regarding a hearing on 9 December at Harbridge County Court.
Lee Whitfield confirmed the claim is a possession claim on rent arrears grounds (ground eight, ten and eleven) by Ashcroft Lettings.
Lee Whitfield stated he has lived in the flat for six years.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he lives alone with a cat.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he offered £50 a month in September, but the landlord rejected it, stating they wanted it all.
Lee Whitfield stated he has the text message of the landlord's rejection on his phone.
Lee Whitfield disclosed there is damp in the bedroom, described as 'black up the wall', and stated he has told the landlord about it and has photos.
Lee Whitfield disclosed other debts including council tax (bailiffs letter), a credit card debt of about £2,000, and electricity on a meter.
Lee Whitfield stated no one is helping him with the debts and he has stopped opening mail.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he went to his GP in March after receiving the first letter regarding arrears.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he took an overdose of 16 paracetamol in March; his neighbour found him and rang an ambulance, resulting in an overnight hospital stay.
Lee Whitfield stated a nurse rang a couple of times after the hospital, then nothing.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he has not hurt himself since March.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he thought about ending his life this week, specifically on Sunday night.
Lee Whitfield confirmed he thought about ending his life on Sunday but did not do anything.
Lee Whitfield stated he is safe today and talking about it helps.
Lee Whitfield disclosed he put the housing costs problem on his Universal Credit journal twice with no answer.
Lee Whitfield stated he has the tenancy agreement, rent statement, Universal Credit statements since January, and damp photos.
Lee Whitfield stated he can email documents by Friday 27th.
Lee Whitfield stated his priority is to not lose the flat.
Lee Whitfield stated he would like a breathing space from creditors.
Lee Whitfield stated he wants to ring his GP together with the solicitor.
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would file a defence and counterclaim regarding the damp.
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would ask the court to adjourn if more time is needed to sort Universal Credit.
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would refer Lee to the Citizens Advice debt team to apply for a breathing space (stops creditors for 60 days).
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would write to Universal Credit regarding the housing costs problem.
Solicitor Sophie Grant stated she would give Lee the crisis team number and Samaritans (116 123).
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would ring Lee on Thursday to check in.
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would file the defence by Tuesday 1st December.
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would ring Lee's GP together with Lee today.
Solicitor Sophie Grant stated she would email documents by Friday 27th.
